extracted.intended_audience: automobile manufacturers, industrial managers, company executives, and vehicle dealers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical criteria for designing, producing, marketing, and supporting mass-market automobiles: material selection and testing, model/standardization strategy, production/mass-manufacturing principles, dealer/agent selection and operation, and advertising/service practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (1) — progressive, up-to-date man
rubrics_metrics.description: A progressive, up-to-date man keenly alive to the possibilities of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first of nine concrete requirements for agents; implies selecting agents who are proactive, forward-looking, and business-minded rather than complacent or traditionalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (2) — suitable place of business
rubrics_metrics.description: A suitable place of business clean and dignified in appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dealers must present a respectable storefront/office; physical presentation is part of sales effectiveness and brand reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (3) — stock of parts sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: A stock of parts sufficient to make prompt replacements and keep in active service every Ford car in his territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes spare-parts availability as essential to customer service and to keeping cars in operation; supports the policy of prompt replacement rather than lengthy repairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (4) — adequately equipped repair shop
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequately equipped repair shop which has in it the right machinery for every necessary repair and adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repair shops must have appropriate tools/machinery to perform all needed repairs; technical capability at the dealer level is required to maintain reliability and customer satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (5) — mechanics familiar with cars
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanics who are thoroughly familiar with the construction and operation of Ford cars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing standard: trained mechanics who know the vehicle's design and operation to perform correct repairs and advise customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (6) — comprehensive bookkeeping and follow-up system
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive bookkeeping system and a follow-up sales system, so that it may be instantly apparent what is the financial status of the various departments of his business, the condition and size of his stock, the present owners of cars, and the future prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard: dealers must maintain proper records and active follow-up to manage inventory, service needs, and customer relationships; enables rapid business decisions and customer service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (7) — absolute cleanliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute cleanliness throughout every department. There must be no unwashed windows, dusty furniture, dirty floors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hygiene and order are considered essential to business dignity and customer confidence; every department must be kept scrupulously clean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (8) — suitable display sign
rubrics_metrics.description: A suitable display sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visibility and branding requirement; dealers must signal legitimacy and attract customers with proper signage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer/agent requirement (9) — policies ensuring square dealing and high ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The adoption of policies which will ensure absolutely square dealing and the highest character of business ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dealers must commit to honest, fair practices; corporate reputation depends on ethical conduct at the dealer level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer solicitation & territory instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: A dealer or a salesman ought to have the name of every possible automobile buyer in his territory, including all those who have never given the matter a thought. He should then personally solicit by visitation if possible—by correspondence at the least—every man on that list and then making necessary memoranda, know the automobile situation as related to every resident so solicited. If your territory is too large to permit this, you have too much territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational sales rubric: exhaustive local prospecting and personal solicitation are required; territories must be sized so dealers can personally contact and track every potential buyer. If territory prevents this, it is too large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay high compensation to secure top service from agents
rubrics_metrics.description: We eventually appointed agents, selecting the very best men we could find, and then paying to them a salary larger than they could possibly earn in business for themselves... paying the very highest reward for service and then insisting upon getting the highest service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment/compensation guideline: pay premium salaries to attract and retain top-performing sales agents, and demand commensurate performance; investing in people is essential to service quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for interchangeability and upgradeability
rubrics_metrics.description: When a model was settled upon then every improvement on that model should be interchangeable with the old model, so that a car should never get out of date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product-design principle: improvements must be backward-compatible/interchangeable to keep existing vehicles current and avoid obsolescence; supports long-term customer investment in the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition for extreme durability (design for no repeat purchase)
rubrics_metrics.description: My ambition to have every piece of machinery, or other non-consumable product that I turn out, so strong and so well made that no one ought ever to have to buy a second one. A good machine of any kind ought to last as long as a good watch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durability as a design goal: non-consumable goods should be built to very high longevity standards; company aims to minimize repeat purchases by maximizing lifetime of product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity in operation (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity in operation—because the masses are not mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design requirement: controls, operation, and maintenance must be simple enough for ordinary users, not specialists; simplicity broadens market and reduces customer support burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality in material to give service in use (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality in material to give service in use. Vanadium steel is the strongest, toughest, and most lasting of steels. It forms the foundation and super-structure of the cars. It is the highest quality steel in this respect in the world, regardless of price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material-quality standard: use the best-suited materials (even costly ones) where durability and performance depend on them; emphasis on investing in superior materials like vanadium steel for critical components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power in sufficient quantity (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power in sufficient quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance criterion: engine and motive systems must provide adequate power for intended uses and terrains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute reliability (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute reliability—because of the varied uses to which the cars would be put and the variety of roads over which they would travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability requirement: vehicles must perform dependably across diverse conditions; supports reputation and market acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lightness / low weight (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lightness. With the Ford there are only 7.95 pounds to be carried by each cubic inch of piston displacement... The lighter the weight, the lighter the expense of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight minimization principle: reduce vehicle weight to improve fuel efficiency, reduce wear, and enable better all-terrain performance; achieved via material selection and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control — safe, easy handling (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control—to hold its speed always in hand, calmly and safely meeting every emergency and contingency either in the crowded streets of the city or on dangerous roads. The planetary transmission of the Ford gave this control and anybody could work it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling and control criterion: transmission and control systems must be intuitive and provide safe manoeuvrability for ordinary drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fuel/operating efficiency through light design (universal car attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: The more a motor car weighs, naturally the more fuel and lubricants are used in the driving; the lighter the weight, the lighter the expense of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational-cost criterion: design choices should lower lifetime operating costs (fuel, oil) by focusing on lightness and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design with few, accessible constructional units (Model T design principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The important feature of the new model...was its simplicity. There were but four constructional units in the car—the power plant, the frame, the front axle, and the rear axle. All of these were easily accessible and they were designed so that no special skill would be required for their repair or replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modular, accessible design requirement: minimize number of major assemblies and make them easily serviceable to reduce skill requirements for repair and simplify manufacturing/assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make parts inexpensive to replace rather than repair
rubrics_metrics.description: The parts could be made so cheaply that the menace of expensive hand repair work would be entirely eliminated. The parts could be carried in hardware shops just as nails or bolts are carried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serviceability/manufacturing guideline: design parts to be cheap and standardized so replacement is economical and parts can be widely stocked (even in general hardware), reducing repair turnaround and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific materials selection and testing (vanadium steel program)
rubrics_metrics.description: We, for the first time I think, in the history of any large construction, determined scientifically the exact quality of the steel. As a result we then selected twenty different types of steel for the various steel parts. About ten of these were vanadium. Vanadium was used wherever strength and lightness were required... By further experimenting, especially in the direction of heat treating, we have been able still further to increase the strength of the steel and therefore to reduce the weight of the car.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials-engineering rubric: empirically test and specify the precise metallurgical properties required for each part; develop or procure appropriate alloys and treatments (e.g., vanadium steel, heat treatment) to meet functional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance parts' strengths to purpose (equal-strength design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The design had to balance. Men die because a part gives out. Machines wreck themselves because some parts are weaker than others. Therefore, a part of the problem in designing a universal car was to have as nearly as possible all parts of equal strength considering their purpose—to put a motor in a one-horse shay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural-design principle: ensure component strengths are harmonized so that no single part is a weak link; design for balanced load distribution and appropriate material choice by function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fool-proofness / responsibility for failures
rubrics_metrics.description: It had to be fool proof... 'When one of my cars breaks down I know I am to blame.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and quality responsibility: aim for designs that are tolerant of misuse and take corporate responsibility for breakdowns—designers and makers must ensure customers can operate vehicles without specialized knowledge, and accept accountability for failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of races and endurance tests as advertising and product validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Winning a race or making a record was then the best kind of advertising... The Scottish Reliability Trials... The Ford came through with only one involuntary stop against it. That started the Ford sales in England... It appeared that we were the under dog and we had the public's sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing tactic and validation method: use performance demonstrations, races, and endurance/reliability trials to build public confidence and advertise durability; stunts and publicized legal or competitive struggles can also generate sympathy and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use financial guarantees to reassure purchasers under litigation threat
rubrics_metrics.description: We...said: we will give them, in addition to the protection of the Ford Motor Company with its some $6,000,000.00 of assets, an individual bond backed by a Company of more than $6,000,000.00 more of assets, so that each and every individual owner of a Ford car will be protected until at least $12,000,000.00 of assets have been wiped out... The bond is yours for the asking, so do not allow yourself to be sold inferior cars at extravagant prices because of any statement made by this 'Divine' body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customer-confidence tactic: offer bonds/guarantees or financial assurances to buyers during periods of legal or market uncertainty to maintain sales and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize on a single model and chassis to reduce costs and increase production
rubrics_metrics.description: In the future we were going to build only one model, that the model was going to be 'Model T,' and that the chassis would be exactly the same for all cars... 'Any customer can have a car painted any colour that he wants so long as it is black.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product-line and manufacturing strategy: reduce variety to a single model and chassis to simplify production, reduce costs, and enable high-volume manufacturing; accept limitations in cosmetic options to gain manufacturing efficiency and lower prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply modern machinery and intelligently directed power to raise output and uniform quality
rubrics_metrics.description: It was the application of these same methods to the making of the Ford car that at the very start lowered the price and heightened the quality... Modern methods applied in a big way have not only brought the cost of axe handles down to a fraction of their former cost—but they have immensely improved the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production principle: employ mechanization, specialization, and process engineering (mass production methods) to simultaneously lower unit cost and improve uniformity/quality of the product.
